agent.result_text:
The late charge is now worked out per 30-day boundary, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works now:** for each full 30 days a claim is overdue, the app takes the late percent in force on that boundary date (due-by plus 30, 60, 90 … days). It charges that percent of the claim's figure, rounded the same way the claim is, and adds the charges up. A boundary where the percent is 0.00 adds nothing. Before, it took the percent in force on the claim's own date and multiplied it by the number of 30-day periods, rounding only once.

The charge is calculated in two places, so I changed both:
- **Server:** `Lateness.charge` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/Lateness.java`. The rollups, statements, settling and re-settling all go through it.
- **Screen:** the browser works out the figures it shows (claim due, person totals, overdue figures) itself. In `features/rates/rates.ts`, `lateCharge` now adds up a charge per boundary. In `features/overdue/overdue.ts`, a new `lateBoundaries` lists the boundary dates, and `lateOf` now looks the percent up by date instead of by claim.

A settled claim still keeps the due that was frozen when it was settled; that already worked, so I didn't change it. No stored data or schema changed. I also updated the comments that described the old rule in `SettingStore`, `SettingsResponse` and `settings.ts`.
